title: Bunk and Lips Page at Ryan's, and Lips in Houston
summary: Lips Page was moved hearing Bunk play at a Ryan's session; Russell adds Lips's Houston tipping story.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I had a lot of trouble up there. Is there anything else about any of the other nights that you remember going around with Bunk to hear music or anyplace else that you ran across him? Not necessarily at Lessons or at the Stuyvesant or someplace where he was playing while you're in this groove about like Ryan's or anyplace else. Do you remember Bunk coming in or Harlem or anyplace else?

I remember Bunk playing at Ryan's, playing beautifully at Ryan's. It was a session, I think it was one of the sessions, the Sunday sessions that Lips Page was usually playing and Bunk came in to sit in. And I remember Lips was standing at the bar and was completely moved. Bunk was playing so beautifully and Lips really did love the way Bunk played, you know. And he wouldn't even play. He wouldn't even get on the bandstand. He says, that's the man, you know. He says, I don't want to play. And it was very good. I think Willie the Lion was playing piano then and the Lion was doing a good job. He was playing for Bunk, you know, very well. Played very well together at that time.

We were talking the other night about Bunk in Texas and I think I told you that, if I remember rightly, that Bunk played at the American Theatre in Houston. And Lips Page was sort of a bellboy or a reporter or whatever you'd call it. But they helped him with the baggage in and out. And he always said the two biggest tippers were Bessie Smith and Bunk. I don't know if Bunk ever just came in and out or stayed there all the time. But anyway, evidently Bunk would give him good tips for helping him. I'm quite sure that was Lips Page.
